# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hassan_2020_meropenem"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hassan_2020_meropenem"))$description`
* Article: [Clin Transl Sci 2020;13(2):301-308](https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12710)

# Population

Hassan 2020 built one population PK model for meropenem across the whole
paediatric age range by pooling two data sources (Methods 'Data'):

* 188 infants of 23-40 weeks gestational age (GA) and 1-92 days postnatal
  age (PNA) with suspected or complicated intra-abdominal infection, whose
  780 serum concentrations from Smith 2011 were obtained from the NICHD
  Pediatric Trials Network data repository; and
* 100 virtual children aged 2-200 months, simulated by the authors from the
  published Du 2006 population model (which already pooled the Blumer 1995
  and Parker 1995 cohorts) because the original data were not available.
  Each virtual child contributed eight concentrations after 20 mg/kg every
  8 hours infused over 30 minutes.

The pooled data set (Table 2) had a median (range) PNA of 0.11 years
(0.002-16.3), GA of 33 weeks (22.5-40; 40 weeks imputed for subjects older
than 120 days), body weight of 2.36 kg (0.39-88.3) and serum creatinine of
0.50 mg/dL (0.1-1.9). The model was fitted with Phoenix NLME (FOCE-ELS).
The same information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hassan_2020_meropenem"))$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment model, proportional error | n/a | Results 'PopPK model development and qualification'; Appendix S1 'Variability models' |
| CL = TVCL (WT/70)^dCLdWT PNA^g/(PNA^g + Age50) SCR^dCLdSCR (GA/40)^dCLdGA exp(eta) | n/a | Results, final-model CL equation |
| CL2 = TVCL2 (WT/70)^dCLdWT PNA^g/(PNA^g + Age50) exp(eta) | n/a | Results, final-model CL2 equation |
| V = TVV (WT/70)^dVdWT exp(eta); V2 = TVV2 (WT/70)^dVdWT exp(eta) | n/a | Results, final-model V and V2 equations |
| CObs = C (1 + eps) | n/a | Results, final-model residual equation |
| `lcl` | log(37.1) L/h | Table 3, TVCL 37.1 L/hour/70 kg |
| `lvc` | log(29.1) L | Table 3, TVV 29.1 L/70 kg |
| `lq` | log(6.10) L/h | Table 3, TVCL2 6.10 L/hour/70 kg |
| `lvp` | log(31.9) L | Table 3, TVV2 31.9 L/70 kg |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 1.20 | Table 3, dCLdWT |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.97 | Table 3, dVdWT |
| `lpna50` | log(0.39) years | Table 3, Age 50 (unit 'y') |
| `lhill` | log(0.27) | Table 3, gamma |
| `e_creat_cl` | -0.25 | Table 3, dCLdSCR |
| `e_ga_cl` | 0.84 | Table 3, dCLdGA |
| `etalcl` | 0.315 | Table 3, intersubject variability CL |
| `etalvc` | 0.186 | Table 3, intersubject variability V |
| `etalq` | 1.14 | Table 3, intersubject variability CL2 |
| `etalvp` | 0.319 | Table 3, intersubject variability V2 |
| `propSd` | 0.38 | Table 3, residual error 'Proportional' |
| Dosing groups and regimens | n/a | Table 1; Table 4 |
| Targets: > 2 mg/L for 75% and > 4 mg/L for 50% of the interval (groups 1-4); > 2 or > 4 mg/L for 40% (groups 5-6) | n/a | Methods 'Simulation for dosing recommendations' |

# Virtual cohort

The authors simulated "each subject group" of their pooled data set; those
covariates are not published. A virtual cohort of 200 subjects per group is
therefore built from the published ranges, with the following assumptions:

* **Groups 1-4 (infants under 3 months).** GA is uniform over 23-32 weeks
  (groups 1-2) or 32-40 weeks (groups 3-4), and PNA uniform over 1-14 days
  (groups 1, 3) or 14-90 days (groups 2, 4), matching the Smith 2011 ranges
  quoted in Methods 'Data'. Birth weight is interpolated from approximate
  median birth weight for GA, and current weight grows 1.5% per day of life;
  both carry 15% log-normal variability. Serum creatinine is uniform over
  0.4-1.0 mg/dL for GA < 32 weeks and 0.2-0.7 mg/dL otherwise.
* **Groups 5-6 (3 months to 17 years).** Age is drawn uniformly within the
  four Du 2006 age bands the authors used (2-14, 14-38, 38-66 and 66-200
  months; truncated below at 3 months). Weight comes from approximate CDC
  median weight-for-age with 15% log-normal variability; serum creatinine is
  uniform between age-dependent limits, with 10% of subjects raised 1.2- to
  3.3-fold, as in Methods 'Data'. GA is 40 weeks. Subjects under 50 kg form
  group 5 and those of 50 kg or more group 6.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20200123)
n_per_group <- 200L

# Approximate median birth weight (kg) by gestational age (weeks).
bw_ga <- data.frame(
  ga = c(23, 26, 28, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40),
  bw = c(0.60, 0.85, 1.10, 1.40, 1.75, 2.20, 2.70, 3.10, 3.40)
)
# Approximate CDC median weight (kg) for age (years), sexes averaged.
wt_age <- data.frame(
  age = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 17),
  wt = c(6.0, 7.6, 9.6, 12.2, 14.3, 16.3, 18.4, 20.7, 25.6, 32.0, 40.5, 50.0, 58.0, 61.0)
)

make_infants <- function(group, ga_lo, ga_hi, pna_lo, pna_hi) {
  ga <- runif(n_per_group, ga_lo, ga_hi)
  pna_d <- runif(n_per_group, pna_lo, pna_hi)
  bw <- approx(bw_ga$ga, bw_ga$bw, xout = ga)$y * exp(rnorm(n_per_group, 0, 0.15))
  creat <- if (ga_hi <= 32) runif(n_per_group, 0.4, 1.0) else runif(n_per_group, 0.2, 0.7)
  tibble(group = group, GA = ga, PNA = pna_d / 30.4375, WT = bw * (1 + 0.015 * pna_d), CREAT = creat)
}

infants <- bind_rows(
  make_infants("Group 1", 23, 32, 1, 14),
  make_infants("Group 2", 23, 32, 14, 90),
  make_infants("Group 3", 32, 40, 1, 14),
  make_infants("Group 4", 32, 40, 14, 90)
)

# Children: a pool in the four Du 2006 age bands (the oldest band
# over-sampled so enough subjects reach 50 kg). Group 5 takes 50 subjects
# under 50 kg from each band; group 6 takes 200 subjects of 50 kg or more.
n_band <- 1500L
bands <- tibble(
  band = 1:4,
  lo = c(3, 14, 38, 66),
  hi = c(14, 38, 66, 204),
  n = c(n_band, n_band, n_band, 3L * n_band)
)
pool <- bands |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(band = band, PNA = runif(n, lo, hi)) |>
  mutate(
    age_yr = PNA / 12,
    GA = 40,
    WT = approx(wt_age$age, wt_age$wt, xout = age_yr, rule = 2)$y *
      exp(rnorm(n(), 0, 0.15)),
    CREAT = runif(n(), 0.20 + 0.02 * age_yr, 0.40 + 0.05 * age_yr),
    outlier = runif(n()) < 0.10,
    CREAT = ifelse(outlier, CREAT * runif(n(), 1.2, 3.3), CREAT)
  )
children <- bind_rows(
  pool |>
    filter(WT < 50) |>
    group_by(band) |>
    slice_head(n = n_per_group / 4) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(group = "Group 5"),
  pool |>
    filter(WT >= 50) |>
    slice_sample(n = n_per_group) |>
    mutate(group = "Group 6")
) |>
  select(group, GA, PNA, WT, CREAT)
stopifnot(nrow(children) == 2 * n_per_group)

cohort <- bind_rows(infants, children)

cohort |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `GA median (weeks)` = median(GA),
    `PNA median (years)` = median(PNA / 12),
    `WT median (kg)` = median(WT),
    `SCR median (mg/dL)` = median(CREAT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Group = group) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual cohort covariates by dosing group.")
```

# Typical-value parameters

The typical-value clearance in a 5-year-old, 18-kg child with serum
creatinine 0.4 mg/dL is about 0.4 L/h/kg, and in a 7-day-old, 1.2-kg
preterm infant (GA 30 weeks, serum creatinine 0.8 mg/dL) about
0.09 L/h/kg, in line with the paediatric meropenem literature the paper
pools.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Hassan_2020_meropenem")

typ_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3, time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
  WT = c(70, 18, 1.2), PNA = c(17 * 12, 5 * 12, 7 / 30.4375),
  GA = c(40, 40, 30), CREAT = c(1, 0.4, 0.8)
)
# One solve per subject: a typical-value solve of several subjects at once
# warns about simulating multiple subjects without between-subject variability.
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ <- lapply(split(typ_ev, typ_ev$id), function(d) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, d))
}) |>
  bind_rows()

# Closed form of the printed equations for the 70-kg, SCR 1 mg/dL, GA 40
# reference adolescent (17 years): only the maturation factor differs from 1.
f17 <- 17^0.27 / (17^0.27 + 0.39)
stopifnot(
  abs(typ$cl[1] / (37.1 * f17) - 1) < 1e-6,
  abs(typ$vc[1] / 29.1 - 1) < 1e-6,
  abs(typ$q[1] / (6.10 * f17) - 1) < 1e-6,
  abs(typ$vp[1] / 31.9 - 1) < 1e-6
)

typ |>
  transmute(
    Subject = c("17 y, 70 kg", "5 y, 18 kg", "7 d, 1.2 kg, GA 30"),
    `CL (L/h/kg)` = cl / typ_ev$WT,
    `V1 (L/kg)` = vc / typ_ev$WT,
    `Q (L/h/kg)` = q / typ_ev$WT,
    `V2 (L/kg)` = vp / typ_ev$WT
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value weight-normalised parameters.")
```

# Simulation

Each group receives the regimens of Table 4: the FDA-approved regimen for
all six groups, and for groups 5 and 6 the three alternatives (doubled dose
every 8 hours; the approved dose every 6 hours; the approved dose infused
over 3 hours instead of 30 minutes). Twenty doses are given and the last
dosing interval is analysed as steady state (Figure 1 legend); the slow
peripheral exchange of preterm infants needs that many doses to reach it.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- tribble(
  ~group,    ~regimen,         ~mgkg, ~cap, ~tau, ~tinf,
  "Group 1", "FDA",               20, 1000,   12,   0.5,
  "Group 2", "FDA",               20, 1000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 3", "FDA",               20, 1000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 4", "FDA",               30, 1000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 5", "FDA",               20, 1000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 5", "Increased dose",    40, 2000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 5", "Q6h",               20, 1000,    6,   0.5,
  "Group 5", "3-h infusion",      20, 1000,    8,   3,
  "Group 6", "FDA",               NA, 1000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 6", "Increased dose",    NA, 2000,    8,   0.5,
  "Group 6", "Q6h",               NA, 1000,    6,   0.5,
  "Group 6", "3-h infusion",      NA, 1000,    8,   3
)

n_dose <- 20L
dt <- 0.05

design <- cohort |>
  mutate(subj = row_number()) |>
  inner_join(regimens, by = "group", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    # Group 6 doses are flat (1 g or 2 g); the others are mg/kg, capped.
    dose = ifelse(is.na(mgkg), cap, pmin(mgkg * WT, cap)),
    treatment = paste(group, regimen, sep = ": ")
  )

doses <- design |>
  cross_join(tibble(dose_n = seq_len(n_dose))) |>
  mutate(
    time = (dose_n - 1) * tau, evid = 1L, amt = dose,
    rate = dose / tinf, cmt = "central"
  )
obs <- design |>
  cross_join(tibble(k = 0:round(12 / dt))) |>
  filter(k * dt <= tau + 1e-9) |>
  mutate(
    time = (n_dose - 1) * tau + k * dt,
    evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, WT, PNA, GA, CREAT, tau, treatment) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200123)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "tau")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, time, Cc, cl, treatment, tau) |>
  left_join(design |> select(id, group, regimen), by = "id") |>
  mutate(tad = time - (n_dose - 1) * tau)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

# Replicate Figure 1: steady-state concentration percentiles

```{r figure1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
fig1 <- sim |>
  filter(regimen == "FDA") |>
  group_by(group, tad) |>
  summarise(
    P50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50), P25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25),
    P10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10), P05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(P50, P25, P10, P05), names_to = "percentile", values_to = "Cc")

ggplot(fig1, aes(tad, Cc, colour = percentile)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(2, 4), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)",
    y = "Meropenem concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "Percentile",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Hassan 2020 (FDA-approved regimens, Table 1)."
  )
```

# Replicate Table 4: target attainment

A subject meets the target when the concentration exceeds the MIC for at
least the target fraction of the steady-state dosing interval: 75% (MIC
2 mg/L) or 50% (MIC 4 mg/L) for groups 1-4, and 40% for groups 5-6.

```{r table4}
ft <- sim |>
  filter(tad < tau) |>
  group_by(id, group, regimen) |>
  summarise(ft2 = mean(Cc > 2), ft4 = mean(Cc > 4), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    infant = group %in% paste("Group", 1:4),
    hit2 = ft2 >= ifelse(infant, 0.75, 0.40),
    hit4 = ft4 >= ifelse(infant, 0.50, 0.40)
  )

pta <- ft |>
  group_by(group, regimen) |>
  summarise(`2` = 100 * mean(hit2), `4` = 100 * mean(hit4), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(`2`, `4`), names_to = "mic", values_to = "PTA")

# Table 4; '> 97.5' is entered as 97.5.
published <- tribble(
  ~group,    ~regimen,          ~mic, ~PTA_published,
  "Group 1", "FDA",              "2",           95.1,
  "Group 1", "FDA",              "4",           95.8,
  "Group 2", "FDA",              "2",           94.2,
  "Group 2", "FDA",              "4",           94.4,
  "Group 3", "FDA",              "2",           94.8,
  "Group 3", "FDA",              "4",           95.7,
  "Group 4", "FDA",              "2",           82.9,
  "Group 4", "FDA",              "4",           86.6,
  "Group 5", "FDA",              "2",           68.4,
  "Group 5", "FDA",              "4",           41.7,
  "Group 5", "Increased dose",   "2",           85.5,
  "Group 5", "Increased dose",   "4",           68.6,
  "Group 5", "Q6h",              "2",           97.5,
  "Group 5", "Q6h",              "4",           94.9,
  "Group 5", "3-h infusion",     "2",           97.5,
  "Group 5", "3-h infusion",     "4",           90.7,
  "Group 6", "FDA",              "2",           41.3,
  "Group 6", "FDA",              "4",           17.0,
  "Group 6", "Increased dose",   "2",           64.7,
  "Group 6", "Increased dose",   "4",           41.2,
  "Group 6", "Q6h",              "2",           93.9,
  "Group 6", "Q6h",              "4",           80.1,
  "Group 6", "3-h infusion",     "2",           94.5,
  "Group 6", "3-h infusion",     "4",           79.6
)

pta_cmp <- published |>
  inner_join(pta, by = c("group", "regimen", "mic")) |>
  mutate(diff = PTA - PTA_published)
stopifnot(nrow(pta_cmp) == nrow(published))

pta_cmp |>
  rename(
    Group = group, Regimen = regimen, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
    "% achieving target, Hassan 2020" = PTA_published,
    "% achieving target, simulated" = PTA,
    "Difference (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Table 4 target attainment: published versus virtual cohort.")
```

```{r table4-gate}
# The FDA-regimen cells are the paper's headline result. The virtual cohort
# approximates the authors' covariates, and each simulated percentage carries
# a binomial SE of up to 3.5 points at n = 200, so the gate is on the centre of
# the twelve differences. A mis-transcribed CL, V, exponent or maturation
# constant moves these percentages by tens of points. Realised: median
# difference -4.6 points, median absolute difference 7.4 points.
fda <- pta_cmp |> filter(regimen == "FDA")
stopifnot(
  abs(median(fda$diff)) < 10,
  median(abs(fda$diff)) < 14
)
```

For the approved regimens the virtual cohort reproduces the paper's
pattern: high target attainment in infants under 3 months, and markedly
lower attainment in children over 3 months, lowest in those of 50 kg or
more. The simulated attainment in the first two weeks of life (groups 1
and 3) runs about 10 points below the published values, which is within
what the assumed neonatal weight and serum creatinine distributions can
shift. Of the alternative regimens, the doubled dose and the 3-hour
infusion are reproduced to within about 12 points. The every-6-hours regimen is not: the simulated attainment for
it is well below the published > 97.5% / 94.9% (group 5) and 93.9% / 80.1%
(group 6), and close to that of the doubled dose, which is what the model
structure implies (shortening the interval from 8 to 6 hours lowers the
required time above the MIC by 0.8 hours; doubling the dose extends the
time above the MIC by about one elimination half-life of 0.7-1 hours). See
Assumptions and deviations.

mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16)

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over the last (twentieth) dosing interval of the FDA-approved
regimen in each group.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(regimen == "FDA", !is.na(Cc), tad <= tau) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- doses |>
  filter(regimen == "FDA", dose_n == n_dose) |>
  transmute(id, time, amt, duration = tinf, treatment)

t_start <- conc_df |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(start = min(time), end = max(time), .groups = "drop")

intervals <- t_start |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             doseu = "mg", duration = "duration")
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res),
             caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA for the FDA-approved regimens.")
```

At steady state the AUC over one dosing interval equals dose / CL for each
subject; the check compares PKNCA's AUC with that identity.

```{r auc-identity}
cl_df <- sim |>
  filter(regimen == "FDA") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), .groups = "drop")

auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, treatment, auclast = PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(cl_df, by = "id") |>
  inner_join(dose_df |> select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / (amt / cl) - 1))

auc_chk |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    `Median % difference` = median(pct_diff),
    `90th percentile of abs % difference` = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Treatment = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PKNCA AUC0-tau versus dose / CL.")

# After twenty doses only the slowest-equilibrating preterm infants fall
# short of steady state, and the 0.05-h trapezoid grid adds a small bias. A dose, unit
# or clearance error shifts every subject by far more than these bounds.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_chk$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(auc_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

The paper reports no NCA parameters, so no published-versus-simulated NCA
table is shown.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Maturation function as printed.** Both the final-model equations in
  the Results and the maturation equation in Appendix S1 write the
  postnatal-age term as PNA^gamma / (PNA^gamma + Age50), with Age50 not
  raised to gamma (the usual Hill form is PNA^gamma / (PNA^gamma +
  Age50^gamma)). The model follows the printed equation. As a consequence
  Age50 (0.39 years) is not literally the age of half-maximal clearance:
  with gamma = 0.27 the maturation factor reaches 0.5 at about 11 days of
  life and 0.67 at 0.39 years.
- **Postnatal-age units.** Table 3 gives Age50 in years ('y') and Table 2
  reports PNA in years, so PNA enters the maturation term in years. Appendix
  S1 describes TM50 'in weeks' while introducing the maturation function for
  the initial analysis of the neonatal data alone; the final-model units of
  Table 3 are used. The package's canonical `PNA` column is in months, and
  `model()` converts with PNA / 12.
- **Serum creatinine and gestational age.** Serum creatinine enters CL
  un-normalised, in mg/dL, as printed, so the typical CL in Table 3 refers to
  serum creatinine 1 mg/dL. Gestational age is normalised to 40 weeks; the
  authors imputed 40 weeks for subjects older than 120 days with missing GA,
  so supply GA = 40 for children when it is unknown.
- **Shared exponents.** One weight exponent (dCLdWT) scales both CL and Q,
  and one (dVdWT) scales both V1 and V2, as the Results describe; the
  maturation term applies to both CL and Q.
- **IIV read as variances.** Table 3 does not label its intersubject
  variability values. They are taken as omega^2 variances of the
  exponential random effects (the quantity Phoenix NLME reports). The
  published target attainment does not discriminate between this reading
  and a standard-deviation reading: both land within the cohort uncertainty
  of Table 4 for the approved regimens. The residual-error entry
  'Proportional (%)' = 0.38 is taken as a proportional SD of 0.38 (38%),
  the only reading consistent with a fraction.
- **Target attainment without residual error.** Time above the MIC is
  computed from the individual predicted concentration; the paper does not
  say whether its simulations added residual error.
- **Virtual cohort.** The authors' per-group covariates are not published.
  The cohort here is built from the published ranges with approximate
  birth-weight-for-GA and CDC weight-for-age medians and assumed serum
  creatinine ranges (see Virtual cohort), so target attainment is an
  approximation of Table 4, not a replication of the authors' simulation.
- **Every-6-hours regimen.** The simulated target attainment for the
  every-6-hours alternative falls well below the published values in both
  groups 5 and 6, whereas the approved regimen, the doubled dose and the
  3-hour infusion are reproduced to within the Monte Carlo and cohort
  uncertainty. The discrepancy is the same under either reading of the IIV
  values and is not explained by the printed model; the paper does not
  describe how its every-6-hours simulations differed from the others.
- **Data provenance.** Of the 288 subjects, 100 are virtual children
  simulated by the authors from the Du 2006 model rather than observed
  patients, so the parameters for children over 3 months partly reflect
  that earlier model.
